title: Splat Towers
description: A worm's-eye photograph of glass towers converging into a summer sky, lifted into about a hundred and seventy thousand real 3D Gaussians. From the original camera it is the photograph, exactly; drag and the camera swings up to six degrees round the towers, so they part from each other and from a distant dome of cloud as real structure, uncovering sky and cumulus painted in behind them, and spring home when you let go. Toward the edges of the frame the picture softens the way a lens does wide open, evenly in every direction. Developed like daylight negative film.
intent: herb asked for gaussian splats, 'reality in the computer'. Reference: herb's ref 2 (factory/reality/herb-refs/2-wormseye-skyscrapers.png), the worm's-eye shot of towers converging into cumulus; genre spec factory/reality/genre-spec.md. Splatting after Kerbl et al., 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering (https://repo-sam.inria.fr/fungraph/3d-gaussian-splatting/), with per-splat texture after Textured Gaussians (https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18625).

sources.author: Davi Rezende (@davirezende)
sources.note: Toronto Financial District, iPhone 12 Pro. Depth from Depth Anything V2 Small (tools/depth/depth_hr.py); baked by tools/depth/bakes/splat-towers/bake.py (each tower rebuilt as RANSAC-fitted facade planes, its truss and cables hung on the facade they attach to) into quantised splats (splats.bin), a 2857x3810 texture (photo.webp, the frame at 2304x3072 with a 12% margin outpainted round it), its depth map (depth.png), which every tower splat's photo lookup is depth-tested against, and a sky plate (plate.webp: the towers painted out with LaMa near the sky's edge and clear deep blue further in), which the dome samples behind every tower.
